title: Staged RBAC v2 cutover playbook: dual-write, backfills, customer comms
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: This ticket coordinates the production migration from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2. Scope includes dual-write implementation, backfill of v2 role bindings, cutover orchestration, audit logging alignment, SSO/SAML assertion mapping validation, and customer communications and support runbooks. Goals: ensure zero-permission regressions for active users, maintain audit continuity for compliance, provide clear rollback and fast mitigation paths, and communicate changes to customers with affected orgs.

Technical approach: 1) Dual-write mode: implement write-through adapter in the authorization service so every change to v1 bindings writes a consistent representation to v2. Dual-write is opt-in per-tenant with feature gate. 2) Backfill: create streaming backfill that consumes existing role binding snapshots and event log (last 90 days) to generate v2 bindings. The backfill runs at reduced rate for low-impact tenants and burst for high-priority enterprise tenants. 3) Canonical mapping: RBAC v2 introduces resource-scoped role templates and admin flags. Mapping rules are defined in the design doc (Confluence link below), including resolution rules for conflicting v1 roles. 4) Audit logging: extend audit pipeline to emit both v1 and v2 labels during dual-write, and add a migration tag so security/ap teams can filter migration-related events. 5) SSO/SAML: update SAML assertion to include new attribute mappings (rbac_role_ids and rbac_role_templates) and validate signature and audience with customer test orgs before cutover. 6) Cutover: staged canary release by org size — internal-only tenants -> beta customers -> enterprise tenants after validation windows.

Safety and observability: - Add authentication/authorization integration tests that assert no regressions for 100 canonical user/role combos. - Monitor: authorization error rate, 403 spike, permission lookup latency, audit log lag, number of mismatched bindings between v1 and v2. Dashboards: Auth-RBAC-Migration, Auth-Errors, AuditLag. - Alerts: 403 rate > baseline + 1% for 30m, audit lag > 5m for 15m, write-failure-rate for v2 > 0.5%. - Canary window: 48 hours for internal -> 72 hours for beta -> 7 days for enterprise.

Backfill strategy: - Phase 1: snapshot export of all org bindings; run dry-run conversion to v2; produce diff report and failing heuristics. - Phase 2: incremental streaming backfill using event-sourced changes; idempotent writes to v2 store. - Phase 3: reconcile pass to detect drift and resolve via conflict resolution policy (prefer most recent last-modified unless marked admin). - Safety: backfill job supports pause, resume, and tombstone handling. Maintain per-org backfill checkpoints in metadata store.

Dual-write design notes: - Implementation in auth-service: implement a writer facade that fans out to v1 store and v2 store. Writes are synchronous to v1 (primary) and asynchronous-retry to v2 with guaranteed at-least-once semantics and conflict detection. - Provide metrics for dual-write success ratio and retry rates. - Expose admin endpoint to force a per-org resync and to flip the feature gate for orgs placed into "v2-only" after cutover.

Cutover and rollback plan: - Pre-cutover checklist: finalize mapping rules, complete end-to-end tests, complete SSO SAML test cycles with 3 pilot customers, run security review, inform legal/compliance. - Cutover steps: 1) enable dual-write for pilot orgs; 2) run backfill and reconcile; 3) validate canary metrics; 4) enable v2 authorization reads for a canary subset; 5) monitor for regressions; 6) progressively expand. - Rollback triggers: spike in 403s, mismatch ratio > 0.2% after reconciliation, audit pipeline errors preventing compliance exports. - Rollback actions: revert authorization reads to v1, keep dual-write enabled to allow v2 fixes, notify customers.

Customer communications and support: - Draft email templates for affected customers explaining the migration, expected impact (none if successful), and testing window. - Publish KB: "RBAC v2 migration: what customers need to know" including SSO attribute changes, admin UI updates, and how to run a role audit. - Runbook for support with common troubleshooting (permission denied after cutover, SAML mapping errors, missing audit events).

Artifacts: Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SEC/RBAC+v2+Mapping+and+Cutover ; Backfill spec: https://docs.redwood.com/backfill/rbac-v2 ; PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-service/pull/1192 ; Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OPS/RBAC+v2+Cutover+Runbook ; Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/abcd1234/auth-rbac-migration

Next steps (short-term): finalize dual-write failure handling (ENG-4812), prioritize SAML pilot orgs (PM-312), schedule migration dry-run on staging (2025-03-08), and finalize customer comms copy by 2025-03-07.
